title: Godot doesn't recognize Blender when installed via snap on Ubuntu
body: ### Tested versions - Godot 4.5.1 ### System information Ubuntu LTS 24.04, Godot 4.5.1, Blender 5.0.1 ### Issue description On Ubuntu LTS24.04 install Godot (4.5.1) and Blender (5.0.1) via snap using the App Center. Importing a project that includes `.blend` files triggers broken dialog that seems to not correctly parse the `blender --version` output. ### Steps to reproduce - Import project with a `.blend` file - A dialog appears to select the Blender executable Bug 1: Using the Browse button to navigate to `/snap/bin/blender` does nothing / the dialog ignore the selected executable. Presumably this is a result of bug 2 below but without any user feedback. Bug 2: Manually inputting the path in the input field produces an error: The output from `/snap/bin/blender` looks as follows: ``` /snap/blender/current/blender --version Blender 5.0.1 build date: 2025-12-16 build time: 01:30:59 build commit date: 2025-12-15 build commit time: 16:36 build hash: a3db93c5b259 build branch: blender-v5.0-release build platform: Linux build type: Release build c -Werror=return-type -Wno-char-subscripts -Wno-unknown-pragmas -Wpointer-arith -Wunused-parameter -Wwrite-strings -Wundef -Wcomma-subscript -Wformat-signedness -Wrestrict -Wno-suggest-override -Wuninitialized -Wno-stringop-overread -Wno-stringop-overflow -Wimplicit-fallthrough=5 -Wundef -Wmissing-declarations -march=x86-64-v2 -pipe -fPIC -funsigned-char -fno-strict-aliasing -ffp-contract=off build link flags: -Wl,--version-script='/home/blender/git/blender-v500/blender.git/source/creator/symbols_unix.map' build system: CMake ``` I've tested to set the Blender path in the editor settings manually and this just means the dialog gets prefilled while still refusing to use Blender ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)
